Tomato___healthy.symptoms: No visible disease symptoms detected. Leaves are vibrant green and spotless.
Tomato___healthy.prevention: Continue regular watering, proper fertilization, and consistent monitoring.

Tomato___Target_Spot.symptoms: Small, circular brown lesions with concentric rings resembling a target on leaves and stems.
treatment: Apply fungicides containing chlorothalonil, mancozeb, or copper products
Prune lower branches to keep foliage off the ground
Tomato___Target_Spot.prevention: Avoid overhead irrigation, rotate crops with non-host species, and maximize air circulation.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.symptoms: Fine white/yellow stippling (tiny dots) on leaves, progressing to yellowing and fine silky webbing on leaf undersides.
treatment: Spray infested plants with insecticidal soap, neem oil, or horticultural oils
Introduce natural predators like predatory mites (Phytoseiidae)
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.prevention: Keep plants well-watered to prevent drought stress, which favors mites; periodically blast leaves with water to dislodge them.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Mottling of light and dark green patches on leaves, leaf distortion, upward curling, or blistering.
treatment: No chemical treatment available; immediately pull and burn/destroy infected plants
Do not compost infected plant debris
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.prevention: Purchase certified disease-free seeds, sanitize gardening tools frequently, and wash hands with soap before handling plants (especially if using tobacco products).

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Numerous small, circular spots with dark brown margins and tan-to-gray centers containing tiny black specks.
treatment: Remove affected lower leaves immediately to stop upward spread
Apply copper-based or chlorothalonil fungicides at the first sign of infection
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.prevention: Always water at the base of the plant, eliminate nightshade weeds, and practice strict 3-year crop rotation.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale green or yellow spots on upper leaf surfaces, with olive-green to grayish-purple velvety mold patches on corresponding undersides.
treatment: Apply calcium chloride-based or copper fungicides thoroughly, focusing on leaf undersides
Aggressively prune lower leaves to reduce relative humidity beneath the canopy
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.prevention: Keep greenhouse humidity below 85%, space plants wide apart, and use resistant varieties if growing indoors.

Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark, concentric-ring 'target' spots on older leaves, leading to yellowing and premature leaf drop.
treatment: Remove and destroy infected leaves immediately
Apply a copper-based, mancozeb, or chlorothalonil fungicide
Tomato___Early_blight.prevention: Rotate crops yearly, use resistant varieties, and apply a thick layer of mulch to prevent soil splashing onto low leaves.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.cause: Virus: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus (TYLCV) transmitted by Whiteflies
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Severe stunting of the plant, with leaves curling dramatically upward and inward, accompanied by distinct yellowing margins.
treatment: No cure for the virus; infected plants must be bagged and discarded immediately to avoid vector spread
Treat remaining plants with systemic insecticides or neem oil to control the insect vectors
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.prevention: Control the whitefly population using yellow sticky traps and insecticidal row covers when plants are young.

Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large, irregular water-soaked dark brown or black lesions on leaves and stems; a white, fuzzy fungal growth appears under wet conditions.
treatment: Instantly destroy the entire infected plant; this disease spreads exceptionally fast via wind
Apply preventative fungicides containing copper, mancozeb, or chlorothalonil to surrounding healthy plants
Tomato___Late_blight.prevention: Avoid overhead watering altogether, monitor weather for cool/wet stretches, and plant in locations with maximal all-day sunlight.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, dark, water-soaked circular spots on leaves that eventually turn necrotic and crack, often surrounded by a faint yellow halo.
treatment: Apply a mixture of copper fungicide and mancozeb weekly during wet spells
Prune and remove infected debris during dry weather only
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Only use certified pathogen-free seeds, avoid working among wet foliage, and eliminate volunteer tomato crops from previous seasons.
